- verify-all: Run the full check + clippy sweep across the workspace AND the WASM plugin (panopt-zellij). Use after non-trivial edits, before declaring work done, or when asked to verify the repo builds cleanly. Captures the dual-target dance (workspace builds for host, panopt-zellij builds only for wasm32-wasip1) so you don't have to remember the right manifest-path/target each time.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

{"id":135,"title":"EPIC: Agent model — types (profiles) → configs (slots) → instances (runs)","body":"Umbrella for refining the agent model into three explicit levels, converged in design discussion 2026-05-31. Tracks the child todos tagged `agent-model`.

## The three levels

1. **Agent types = data (profiles), not code.** A type is a *profile row* that drives a fixed set of generic interpreters; `tool_type` becomes a key into a profile registry. There is no per-type code in the common case.
   - **Launch is data**: a spawn-spec template — `argv` template + `env` map + `files`-to-materialize — over a fixed placeholder set (`{agent_id, name, token, mcp_url, project_path, cwd, model, …}`). env-vs-flag-vs-config-file are just *where a placeholder lands*, not different mechanisms. One substitution engine, not a branch per type.
   - **Status is data**: pattern rules (`thinking/idle/waiting/done`) over agent output, run by one generic pattern engine.
   - **Irreducibly code** (fixed, generic, never per-type): the interpreters (substitution, pattern, health/pane-death) and the placeholder providers (the code that produces `token`/`mcp_url`/`agent_id`). New per-type code is needed only for a genuinely new *step kind* the interpreters can't express — rare, and reusable as data once added.
   - **Scope**: global, layered — shipped-defaults file ← machine/user overrides. Distinct from per-project `agent_tools`.

2. **Agent configs = per-project durable slots** (`agent_tools`, shipped in #27). Reference a type; hold name, cwd, command/arg overrides, system prompt, `enabled`. A slot is a lifecycle-managed line in the project's agents pane.

3. **Agent instances = per-project ephemeral runs** (`processes`, shipped in #27 with reserved `pid/status/agent_state/last_seen`). Reference a config; one per config (1:1 policy, N:1 door left open). Born on start, die on stop.

## Why config and instance stay separate even at 1:1
They are *desired state vs. running state* (spec/status): config = what you want, instance = what's happening, and they legitimately diverge (edited-but-not-restarted, crashed, never-started). Decisively, run-level identity is needed so **sessions (#113) and plans (#105) attach to a run, not the durable slot**. The 1:1 keeps the *UI* one-row-per-slot regardless.

## Relationship to existing todos
- #27 (config/instance schema split) — **schema + MCP surface shipped**; remaining wiring lives in the `tool_type → profile` child. Recommend verifying and closing #27.
- #83 (declared-identity registry) — the registry is the *runtime presence* of an instance; the liveness child must consume it, not re-model liveness.
- #111 (monitor agent status in pane) — **absorbed** by the lifecycle-UI child.
- #105 (plans), #113 (sessions) — downstream consumers; this work gives them a run to attach to.

{"id":141,"title":"Instance lifecycle: panoptd owns the lifecycle record + spawn plan; plugin reconciles into panes","body":"DESIGN §10 lifecycle ownership: panoptd owns *what should be running*; the actual pane is created inside the Zellij session, not by the daemon.

## Who actually spawns (resolved 2026-05-31)
panoptd cannot spawn into a pane — it is a headless HTTP daemon, bound `0.0.0.0` (#80) and reachable cross-machine, with no terminal. The only code that can create a pane is the **panopt-zellij plugin** (`open_command_pane`/`CommandToRun`, plugin-API only, runs inside the session). So three layers:
1. **Zellij** does the literal fork/exec and owns the pane's process.
2. **The plugin** instructs Zellij to spawn (it already runs a reconcile loop — `ingest_panes`, slot mgmt). It is the effector.
3. **panoptd** owns the lifecycle *record* + the resolved *plan* — the desired state — never the act.

Note: panes run **`panopt <subcommand>`** (the wrapper at main.rs:1925, `path: panopt_bin`), not the agent binary directly. The wrapper injects identity/token/mcp-config and execs the real agent, and is the per-instance control seam (reports pid, handles stop, triggers `_agent-leave` on exit).

## Model: daemon decides, plugin reconciles, Zellij execs
- `process_start(#config)`: panoptd validates 1:1, resolves the spawn plan via the spawn-spec interpreter (#137 → argv/env/files), writes a `processes` row in `starting` (copy config's command/cwd into the row per §6.6 copy-on-spawn).
- The **plugin reconciles** the `starting` row into a pane via `open_command_pane`, then reports pid/pane-id back; panoptd flips status to `running`. Rides the plugin's existing poll of daemon state — no new push channel. This inverts today's flow (plugin decides ad hoc → daemon infers liveness) into (daemon resolves plan → plugin effects it).

## Stop is NOT symmetric with start
Invariant: *the plugin never closes panes, only suppresses them.* So `process_stop(#N)` kills the **process** (signal the pid, or tell the in-pane `panopt` wrapper to exit) and leaves the **pane** standing, user-owned, showing the exited command. panopt owns *processes*; Zellij/the user owns *panes*. Do not make the plugin close a pane on stop.

## Co-location constraint
Spawn and kill require an effector where the Zellij session lives. A remote MCP caller can request `process_start`, but the pane is created by the local cockpit/plugin attached to that project's session; with none attached the row stays `starting` (pending) rather than spawning — no terminal to host an interactive pane. The machine-local profile layer (#136 binary path) must resolve on the *executing* host, not the daemon's — moot when co-located, a wrinkle for remote.

## kind split
Only `kind='command'` (headless service) is something panoptd *could* fork and supervise directly. `agent`/`terminal` are interactive and must be panes — plugin-spawned, always.

## 1:1 policy
Starting a config that already has a live instance is a no-op/focus, not a second spawn (N:1 door left closed for now).

## Acceptance
- Starting a config produces a running process and a `processes` row that transitions `starting → running` with a live pid/pane-id; stopping it kills the process and flips runtime columns, pane left standing.
- Resolved spawn plan matches what the plugin previously hand-built for a claude-code pane (no behavior regression).
- No-cockpit-attached start parks the row in `starting` rather than failing hard.

Blocked by the spawn interpreter (#137) and the tool_type→profile wiring (#139). Blocks liveness reporting (#142) and the lifecycle UI (#143). Gives #105/#113 a run to attach to. Part of EPIC #135 (agent-model). 1	//! Agent-type profiles - the top of PANopt's three-level agent model.
2	//!
3	//! A *type* (claude-code, codex, ...) is pure data: a [`AgentProfile`] that
4	//! parameterizes generic interpreters rather than carrying per-type code. The
5	//! [`AgentProfile::spawn`] half is a template the spawn interpreter (a later
6	//! step) renders into a concrete `(argv, env, files)` launch; the
7	//! [`AgentProfile::status`] half is regexes the status interpreter matches
8	//! against an agent's output. New types that fit this shape are new rows in the
9	//! TOML, not new code.
10	//!
11	//! Profiles are *not* project resources: they are global, referenced by a
12	//! `tool_type` string (not a `#N` id), and live in files rather than SQLite -
13	//! keeping them out of the unified per-project id namespace. Two layers merge,
14	//! both global:
15	//!
16	//! 1. **Shipped defaults** - `defaults.toml`, compiled in via [`include_str!`].
17	//!    claude-code lives here. Travels with the binary; the DB cannot ship
18	//!    default rows without a seed migration.
19	//! 2. **User override** - `<config-dir>/panopt/agent-types.toml`, absent by
20	//!    default. `config_dir()` holds user config (matching the cockpit's
21	//!    `viewstate`), as opposed to `data_dir()` which holds runtime state.
22	//!
23	//! The merge is keyed by `tool_type`: an override can add a new type or amend a
24	//! shipped one. Within a profile, **scalars override, maps (`env`, `files`,
25	//! status `patterns`) merge by inner key, and lists (`argv`, each pattern list)
26	//! replace wholesale** - so a user can repoint a binary (scalar), add one env
27	//! var (map-merge), or swap a command line (list-replace) without restating the
28	//! rest. This falls out of a generic deep-merge of the TOML tables: tables
29	//! recurse, everything else replaces.
30	//!
31	//! Placeholders are validated at load (fail-fast): every `{{name}}` in a spawn
32	//! template must be a [`KNOWN_PLACEHOLDERS`] entry or a `{{file:NAME}}` whose
33	//! `NAME` is a key in that profile's `files`. A typo fails the daemon at
34	//! startup rather than at spawn time.
35	
36	use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
37	use std::path::PathBuf;
38	
39	use serde::Deserialize;
40	
41	mod render;
42	mod status;
43	pub use render::{build_launch, Facts, Launch, RenderError};
44	pub use status::{StatusError, StatusMatcher};
45	
46	/// The shipped default profile set, compiled into the binary.
47	const DEFAULTS_TOML: &str = include_str!("defaults.toml");
48	
49	/// The profile a config defaults to when none is chosen, and the key the V11
50	/// migration rewrites the legacy `tool_type='agent'` sentinel to. Lives here so
51	/// the default agent type is named in exactly one place (db.rs binds it, the
52	/// handler falls back to it, the read-time safety net maps stale values onto

input.content:
# #141 — Instance lifecycle: daemon owns the record, plugin reconciles into panes

## Context

EPIC #135 splits the agent model into types (profiles) → configs (slots) → instances (runs). The data/profile foundation is merged: profile schema/loader (#136), the spawn-spec interpreter `build_launch` (#137), the status interpreter (#138), and `tool_type → profile` validation (#139). But nothing yet *spawns* an instance from that machinery.

Today a cockpit agent is spawned ad-hoc: the plugin hand-builds `panopt _agent --id cockpit-agent-N`, and that wrapper hardcodes the claude invocation (`crates/panopt/src/agent.rs:79-90`). There is no `processes` row, no lifecycle state, nothing for plans (#105) or sessions (#113) to attach to.

This todo inverts the flow into **daemon decides → plugin reconciles → Zellij execs**:
- `process_start(#config)` writes a `processes` row in `starting` (desired state).
- The plugin's existing 1s poll reconciles any `starting` row into a Zellij pane.
- The pane runs a `panopt` wrapper that resolves the spawn plan **at the edge** via `build_launch` and execs it, then reports its pid → daemon flips `starting → running`.
- `process_stop(#N)` kills the process but **leaves the pane standing** (invariant: the plugin never closes panes).

**Key architectural decision — `build_launch` runs at the edge, not in the daemon.** The `claude-code` profile (`defaults.toml`) renders `{{panopt_bin}}`, `{{token}}`, `{{ws}}` into a temp MCP-config file — all host-local facts the daemon cannot know for a remote executing host. `build_launch`'s `Facts` (`render.rs:29-72`) is built from `std::env::current_exe()` + the on-disk token, so it must resolve where the pane runs. The daemon owns the lifecycle *record* (config ref, copy-on-spawn command/cwd, status, pid, pane_id); the literal argv/env is resolved in the wrapper at exec time. This is exactly why #137 was built as a callable interpreter rather than wired into the daemon, and it makes the co-location constraint fall out for free.

Decisions confirmed with the user:
- **Trigger surface:** MCP tools + `panopt process start/stop` CLI only. The existing `n` ad-hoc keybinding is left untouched (that rewire is #143).
- **Report scope:** wrapper reports pid (flips to `running`); plugin reports the Zellij pane-id best-effort. Persist a `pane_id` column.

## Status vocabulary

`processes.status` is currently a nullable free string. Centralize the literals in `panopt-core` (e.g. a `process_status` module of `&str` consts or a small enum): `starting`, `running`, `stopped`, `exited`. Keep the DB column a plain string (no CHECK) to stay forward-only. `exited` (pane death) is owned by #142 — define the constant but don't drive it here.

## Implementation

### 1. `panopt-core` — schema + lifecycle methods (`db.rs`, `state.rs`, `model.rs`, `projection.rs`)

- **V12 migration** in `db.rs`: `ALTER TABLE processes ADD COLUMN pane_id TEXT`. New forward-only `V12` block + `if version < 12` step (per the forward-only invariant). Add the `pane_id` read to `process_list`/`fetch_process` (`state.rs:1025,1147`).
- **`model.rs`:** add `pane_id: Option<String>` to `Process` (line ~ struct) and `pane_id: Option<Option<String>>` to `ProcessPatch` (324-337), mirroring the existing nested-Option pattern for pid/status.
- **`state.rs` new methods:**
  - `process_start(&mut self, project, agent_tool_id: u64) -> Result<Process>` — fetch the config via `fetch_agent_tool`; error if missing/disabled. **1:1 policy:** scan `process_list` for a non-deleted row with this `agent_tool_id` and `status ∈ {starting, running}`; if found, return it unchanged (no-op/focus, N:1 door left closed). Otherwise allocate id via `next_id`, insert a row: `kind='agent'`, copy `name`/`display_name`/`command`/`cwd` from the config (copy-on-spawn, §6.6), `agent_tool_id` set, `status='starting'`, `position`. Reproject; return the `Process`.
  - `process_stop(&mut self, project, id: u64) -> Result<()>` — fetch; if `pid` is set, send `SIGTERM` (libc `kill`; co-located best-effort, ignore ESRCH). Patch `status='stopped'`. **Do not touch the pane.** Reproject.
  - `process_report(&mut self, project, id, pid: Option<i64>, pane_id: Option<String>, agent_state: Option<String>) -> Result<()>` — apply a `ProcessPatch` setting whichever fields are present; if `pid` is being set, also set `status='running'` and `last_seen=now`. Reproject. (Two reporters — wrapper sets pid, plugin sets pane_id — both land via this method idempotently.)
- **`projection.rs` `render_processes_md` (254-281):** append status so the plugin can reconcile off the projection. Extend the line to `- [<kind>] #<id> <label> [(from #N)] [· <status>]` — append ` · <status>` only when status is set, preserving the existing prefix the plugin already parses. Update the doc comment and the existing tests (`projection.rs:828`, `state.rs:3184`).

### 2. `panopt-tool-surface` + `panoptd` — MCP surface (`lib.rs`, `handler.rs`)

Follow the one-tool-surface invariant: each new tool is one `ToolDef` in `TOOL_SURFACE` + one `Parameters<T>` struct + one `Tool` enum variant + one `dispatch_local` arm + one `Handler` method.

- **`tool-surface/src/lib.rs`:** add `ProcessStartArgs { agent_tool_id }`, `ProcessStopArgs { process_id }`, `ProcessReportArgs { process_id, pid?, pane_id?, agent_state? }`, plus their `TOOL_SURFACE` rows (mirror the existing `process_*` entries at lib.rs:324-353).
- **`panoptd/src/handler.rs`:** `Tool::ProcessStart/ProcessStop/ProcessReport` variants (1410+), `from_name` arms (1460+), `dispatch_local` arms (1687+), and three `Handler` methods (mirror `process_create` at 1289-1310) calling the new core methods. `handler::tests::tool_enum_covers_tool_surface` enforces coverage automatically.

### 3. `panopt` CLI — edge resolver + report subcommands (`main.rs`, `process.rs`, `agent.rs`/new)

- **Extend `_process-run` (`process.rs:138 exec_entry`)** — the seam the plugin already spawns into a pane:
  - Fetch the process row (`process_get`). If it has an `agent_tool_id`: fetch the config (`agent_tool_get`) for its `tool_type`; `ProfileSet::load()` and `get(tool_type)` the profile; build `Facts` (`panopt_bin = current_exe()`, host/port, `ws`, `project` via `project_identity::resolve`, `agent_id`/`name` from the row name, `token` from disk, `model` from profile default) — reusing the exact value sources in `agent.rs:57-77`; call `build_launch(profile, &facts, tmp_dir)`.
  - **Report pid before exec:** one-shot MCP `process_report { process_id, pid: std::process::id() }` (model on `agent.rs:108 leave()`). `exec` preserves the pid, so the claude child inherits it — this flip to `running` is the liveness anchor.
  - `exec` the resolved `Launch.argv` with `Launch.env`.
  - If the row has **no** `agent_tool_id`: keep the existing bare-`/bin/sh` behavior (command/terminal kinds) unchanged.
- **New hidden `_process-report` subcommand** (`main.rs` clap enum, `_`-prefixed `hide=true`, convention at main.rs:213): `--id <process_id> --pane-id <n>` → one-shot MCP `process_report { process_id, pane_id }`. The plugin shells this after spawning.
- **`panopt process` user CLI (`process.rs:24 ProcessCmd`):** add `Start { config_id }` → `process_start` and `Stop { id }` → `process_stop`, wired in `dispatch`.

### 4. `panopt-zellij` + `panopt-zellij-logic` — plugin reconcile (`lib.rs`, `main.rs`)

- **`panopt-zellij-logic/src/lib.rs`:** add `status: Option<String>` to `ProcessRow` and parse the trailing ` · <status>` in `parse_process_line` (650). Add unit tests for the new field (this crate is where the parser is testable on the host).
- **`panopt-zellij/src/main.rs` reconcile:** in `rebuild_items`/the timer path, for each `ProcessRow` with `status == "starting"` that this cockpit has not already spawned, call `spawn_in_slot(vec!["_process-run", "--id", id])` (1930) and record `process_id → PaneId` in a new map mirroring `agent_pane_ids` (168) for idempotency (don't re-spawn). After spawn, best-effort `run_panopt(["_process-report", "--id", id, "--pane-id", tid])` to report the Zellij pane-id.
  - **No-cockpit-attached** falls out: with no plugin running, nobody reconciles, the row stays `starting` (acceptance criterion).
  - Pane-death → `exited` and de-dup against the registry are **#142's** scope; here just ensure no infinite respawn (a `stopped`/`exited`/`running`-with-recorded-id row is not re-spawned).

## Files (representative)

- `crates/panopt-core/src/{db.rs, state.rs, model.rs, projection.rs}`
- `crates/panopt-tool-surface/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/panoptd/src/handler.rs`
- `crates/panopt/src/{main.rs, process.rs, agent.rs}`
- `crates/panopt-zellij-logic/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/panopt-zellij/src/main.rs`

## Verification

1. **Build both targets:** the `verify-all` skill (workspace `cargo check`/`clippy -D warnings` + the wasm plugin via `--manifest-path crates/panopt-zellij/Cargo.toml --target wasm32-wasip1`).
2. **Unit tests:** `cargo test -p panopt-core` (projection format, process_start 1:1, status transitions) and `cargo test -p panopt-zellij-logic` (parse_process_line status).
3. **End-to-end (`just refresh` to reload daemon + plugin):**
   - `panopt agent-tool add claude-code my-agent` (a config), then `panopt process start #<config>` → confirm a `processes` row appears in `starting` (`panopt process list`).
   - In an attached cockpit, watch the plugin spawn a pane running claude; confirm the row flips to `running` with a live `pid` (and `pane_id`) via `panopt process get #<N>`. Confirm the spawned claude has working panopt MCP tools (no-regression vs the old `_agent` path).
   - `panopt process stop #<N>` → claude exits, the pane stays standing showing the exited command, row status `stopped`.
   - With **no** cockpit attached, `process start` parks the row in `starting` (no spawn, no error).

## Out of scope (other #135 children)

- Pane-death → `exited` liveness + registry reconcile → **#142**.
- Start/stop buttons, status badges, rewiring the `n` key → **#143**.
- Config management form / type dropdown → **#140**.

This todo inverts the flow into **daemon decides → plugin reconciles → Zellij execs**:
- `process_start(#config)` writes a `processes` row in `starting` (desired state).
- The plugin's existing 1s poll reconciles any `starting` row into a Zellij pane.

- `process_stop(#N)` kills the process but **leaves the pane standing** (invariant: the plugin never closes panes).

# #141 — Instance lifecycle: daemon owns the record, plugin reconciles into panes

## Context

EPIC #135 splits the agent model into types (profiles) → configs (slots) → instances (runs). The data/profile foundation is merged: profile schema/loader (#136), the spawn-spec interpreter `build_launch` (#137), the status interpreter (#138), and `tool_type → profile` validation (#139). But nothing yet *spawns* an instance from that machinery.

Today a cockpit agent is spawned ad-hoc: the plugin hand-builds `panopt _agent --id cockpit-agent-N`, and that wrapper hardcodes the claude invocation (`crates/panopt/src/agent.rs:79-90`). There is no `processes` row, no lifecycle state, nothing for plans (#105) or sessions (#113) to attach to.

This todo inverts the flow into **daemon decides → plugin reconciles → Zellij execs**:
- `process_start(#config)` writes a `processes` row in `starting` (desired state).
- The plugin's existing 1s poll reconciles any `starting` row into a Zellij pane.
- The pane runs a `panopt` wrapper that resolves the spawn plan **at the edge** via `build_launch` and execs it, then reports its pid → daemon flips `starting → running`.
- `process_stop(#N)` kills the process but **leaves the pane standing** (invariant: the plugin never closes panes).

**Key architectural decision — `build_launch` runs at the edge, not in the daemon.** The `claude-code` profile (`defaults.toml`) renders `{{panopt_bin}}`, `{{token}}`, `{{ws}}` into a temp MCP-config file — all host-local facts the daemon cannot know for a remote executing host. `build_launch`'s `Facts` (`render.rs:29-72`) is built from `std::env::current_exe()` + the on-disk token, so it must resolve where the pane runs. The daemon owns the lifecycle *record* (config ref, copy-on-spawn command/cwd, status, pid, pane_id); the literal argv/env is resolved in the wrapper at exec time. This is exactly why #137 was built as a callable interpreter rather than wired into the daemon, and it makes the co-location constraint fall out for free.

Decisions confirmed with the user:
- **Trigger surface:** MCP tools + `panopt process start/stop` CLI only. The existing `n` ad-hoc keybinding is left untouched (that rewire is #143).
- **Report scope:** wrapper reports pid (flips to `running`); plugin reports the Zellij pane-id best-effort. Persist a `pane_id` column.

## Status vocabulary

`processes.status` is currently a nullable free string. Centralize the literals in `panopt-core` (e.g. a `process_status` module of `&str` consts or a small enum): `starting`, `running`, `stopped`, `exited`. Keep the DB column a plain string (no CHECK) to stay forward-only. `exited` (pane death) is owned by #142 — define the constant but don't drive it here.

## Implementation

### 1. `panopt-core` — schema + lifecycle methods (`db.rs`, `state.rs`, `model.rs`, `projection.rs`)

- **V12 migration** in `db.rs`: `ALTER TABLE processes ADD COLUMN pane_id TEXT`. New forward-only `V12` block + `if version < 12` step (per the forward-only invariant). Add the `pane_id` read to `process_list`/`fetch_process` (`state.rs:1025,1147`).
- **`model.rs`:** add `pane_id: Option<String>` to `Process` (line ~ struct) and `pane_id: Option<Option<String>>` to `ProcessPatch` (324-337), mirroring the existing nested-Option pattern for pid/status.
- **`state.rs` new methods:**
  - `process_start(&mut self, project, agent_tool_id: u64) -> Result<Process>` — fetch the config via `fetch_agent_tool`; error if missing/disabled. **1:1 policy:** scan `process_list` for a non-deleted row with this `agent_tool_id` and `status ∈ {starting, running}`; if found, return it unchanged (no-op/focus, N:1 door left closed). Otherwise allocate id via `next_id`, insert a row: `kind='agent'`, copy `name`/`display_name`/`command`/`cwd` from the config (copy-on-spawn, §6.6), `agent_tool_id` set, `status='starting'`, `position`. Reproject; return the `Process`.
  - `process_stop(&mut self, project, id: u64) -> Result<()>` — fetch; if `pid` is set, send `SIGTERM` (libc `kill`; co-located best-effort, ignore ESRCH). Patch `status='stopped'`. **Do not touch the pane.** Reproject.
  - `process_report(&mut self, project, id, pid: Option<i64>, pane_id: Option<String>, agent_state: Option<String>) -> Result<()>` — apply a `ProcessPatch` setting whichever fields are present; if `pid` is being set, also set `status='running'` and `last_seen=now`. Reproject. (Two reporters — wrapper sets pid, plugin sets pane_id — both land via this method idempotently.)
- **`projection.rs` `render_processes_md` (254-281):** append status so the plugin can reconcile off the projection. Extend the line to `- [<kind>] #<id> <label> [(from #N)] [· <status>]` — append ` · <status>` only when status is set, preserving the existing prefix the plugin already parses. Update the doc comment and the existing tests (`projection.rs:828`, `state.rs:3184`).

### 2. `panopt-tool-surface` + `panoptd` — MCP surface (`lib.rs`, `handler.rs`)

Follow the one-tool-surface invariant: each new tool is one `ToolDef` in `TOOL_SURFACE` + one `Parameters<T>` struct + one `Tool` enum variant + one `dispatch_local` arm + one `Handler` method.

- **`tool-surface/src/lib.rs`:** add `ProcessStartArgs { agent_tool_id }`, `ProcessStopArgs { process_id }`, `ProcessReportArgs { process_id, pid?, pane_id?, agent_state? }`, plus their `TOOL_SURFACE` rows (mirror the existing `process_*` entries at lib.rs:324-353).
- **`panoptd/src/handler.rs`:** `Tool::ProcessStart/ProcessStop/ProcessReport` variants (1410+), `from_name` arms (1460+), `dispatch_local` arms (1687+), and three `Handler` methods (mirror `process_create` at 1289-1310) calling the new core methods. `handler::tests::tool_enum_covers_tool_surface` enforces coverage automatically.

### 3. `panopt` CLI — edge resolver + report subcommands (`main.rs`, `process.rs`, `agent.rs`/new)

- **Extend `_process-run` (`process.rs:138 exec_entry`)** — the seam the plugin already spawns into a pane:
  - Fetch the process row (`process_get`). If it has an `agent_tool_id`: fetch the config (`agent_tool_get`) for its `tool_type`; `ProfileSet::load()` and `get(tool_type)` the profile; build `Facts` (`panopt_bin = current_exe()`, host/port, `ws`, `project` via `project_identity::resolve`, `agent_id`/`name` from the row name, `token` from disk, `model` from profile default) — reusing the exact value sources in `agent.rs:57-77`; call `build_launch(profile, &facts, tmp_dir)`.
  - **Report pid before exec:** one-shot MCP `process_report { process_id, pid: std::process::id() }` (model on `agent.rs:108 leave()`). `exec` preserves the pid, so the claude child inherits it — this flip to `running` is the liveness anchor.
  - `exec` the resolved `Launch.argv` with `Launch.env`.
  - If the row has **no** `agent_tool_id`: keep the existing bare-`/bin/sh` behavior (command/terminal kinds) unchanged.
- **New hidden `_process-report` subcommand** (`main.rs` clap enum, `_`-prefixed `hide=true`, convention at main.rs:213): `--id <process_id> --pane-id <n>` → one-shot MCP `process_report { process_id, pane_id }`. The plugin shells this after spawning.
- **`panopt process` user CLI (`process.rs:24 ProcessCmd`):** add `Start { config_id }` → `process_start` and `Stop { id }` → `process_stop`, wired in `dispatch`.

### 4. `panopt-zellij` + `panopt-zellij-logic` — plugin reconcile (`lib.rs`, `main.rs`)

- **`panopt-zellij-logic/src/lib.rs`:** add `status: Option<String>` to `ProcessRow` and parse the trailing ` · <status>` in `parse_process_line` (650). Add unit tests for the new field (this crate is where the parser is testable on the host).

After spawn, best-effort `run_panopt(["_process-report", "--id", id, "--pane-id", tid])` to report the Zellij pane-id.
  - **No-cockpit-attached** falls out: with no plugin running, nobody reconciles, the row stays `starting` (acceptance criterion).

#141 is implemented and verified end-to-end on the daemon/CLI side. Here's the summary.

## What landed

The instance lifecycle now flows **daemon decides → plugin reconciles → Zellij execs**, exactly as #141 specified.

**`panopt-core`** — `process_start` (copy-on-spawn `starting` row, 1:1 policy), `process_report` (pid → `running` + `last_seen`; pane_id independent), `process_stop` (flips to `stopped`, returns pid for the caller to signal, pane untouched). V12 migration adds `pane_id`. Status literals centralized in `model::process_status`. Projection appends ` · <status>`.

**`panopt-tool-surface` + `panoptd`** — `process_start`/`process_stop`/`process_report` MCP tools (args, `Tool` variants, dispatch, handlers). Stop's SIGTERM lives in the daemon (`signal_terminate`, new `libc` dep) so core stays pure.

**`panopt` CLI** — `_process-run` now resolves the spawn plan **at the edge** via `build_launch` for agent-backed rows (host-local facts: `current_exe`, on-disk token, daemon host/port) and reports its pid before `exec` (the pid survives into claude). New `_process-report` (plugin → pane-id) and user-facing `panopt process start/stop`.

**`panopt-zellij(-logic)`** — `ProcessRow.status` + parser; the **Todos gatekeeper** reconciles `starting` rows into `_process-run` panes exactly once (`reconciled_panes` guard), then reports the pane-id. Stop is not reconciled — the pane is left standing.

## Verification

- `just check` + `just clippy` (`-D warnings`): **PASS** on both workspace and the wasm plugin.
- `cargo test --workspace`: **327 passed** (new core lifecycle + 1:1 + projection tests; new logic parser tests).

The pid→`running` flip is unit-tested and shares the verified `process_report` plumbing.

content.text:
`<config>` is the numeric id of an **agent config** — an `agent_tools` row (the durable "slot" layer from #27). `process start` takes that config's id and spawns an instance of it.

You get one by creating a config, then referencing its id:

```
panopt agent-tool add mediator --tool-type claude-code --display-name "Mediator"
   → created agent tool #1

panopt agent-tool list
   → #1  Mediator [enabled]

panopt process start 1          # ← the "1" is <config>
   → started process #2 (starting) from config #1
```

So in my e2e it was `#1` (the Mediator config). The `process_start` MCP tool calls it `agent_tool_id`; the CLI positional is `config_id`.

A couple of related notes:
- It must be an **agent config id**, not a process/todo/note id — they all share the one per-project `#N` counter, so `#1` here is the config and `#2` is the running instance it produced.
- Right now configs are created via the CLI (`panopt agent-tool add`) or MCP (`agent_tool_create`). The **cockpit form** to create/edit configs with a type dropdown is #140 — still open — so until then the CLI is how you mint a `<config>`.
